expectations.text: Describes the §127.12 VSD process: prompt initial notification to DDTC, thorough internal investigation, then a full report with facts, causes, remediation
expectations.evidence: "DDTC's Voluntary Self-Disclosure (VSD) process" / "(22 CFR 127.12)": initial notification letter, "internal investigation to scope", full report with "detailed narrative... root cause analysis... remediation plan".

expectations.text: States VSD is a significant mitigating factor and can result in no penalty, warning letter, or reduced civil penalty
expectations.evidence: "generally treated as a strong mitigating factor"; response range "from a closing letter with no further action, to negotiated administrative penalties" with favorable treatment for voluntary disclosure.

expectations.text: Cites current penalty exposure: civil penalties up to ~$1.37M per violation (annually adjusted) and criminal exposure up to $1M/20 years per violation
expectations.evidence: No civil (~$1.37M per violation) or criminal ($1M/20 years) penalty figures cited.

expectations.text: Advises immediate steps: stop the violating activity, preserve records, consider disclosure counsel, review for related EAR/OFAC issues
expectations.evidence: "halt any further unauthorized transfers, shipments, technical data disclosures"; "Issue a litigation/compliance hold"; "legal counsel (ideally outside export control counsel)"; "assess potential overlap with Commerce/BIS (EAR) jurisdiction".

expectations.text: Mentions submissions run through DDTC's DECCS platform (which deployed its Data Collection Modernization release in September 2026)
expectations.evidence: Only "per current DDTC electronic filing guidance" — DECCS and the September 2026 Data Collection Modernization release never mentioned.
